name: Independent on Sunday cryptic crossword No 1,361

clue.text: Putting aside bathroom activity, not hard

indicators.note: 'not hard' asks for the hard abbreviation to be taken out of the activity

blocks.note: what many people do at the bathroom mirror each morning
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Someone skipping their usual bathroom routine because it is too much bother.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the H out of SHAVING to leave SAVING.
explanation.definitionFit: Saving money means setting it by for later rather than spending it.

clue.text: Bogus, an individual claiming spiritual contacts

blocks.note: a sham is a fake or pretence
taken as written

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a fraudulent medium who says they talk to the spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: A shaman is a tribal healer or priest believed to communicate with the spirit world.

clue.text: Battle to eat food -- I restrict my diet

indicators.note: something that eats another thing takes it inside itself, so one word swallows the other

blocks.note: to vie is to compete or struggle
an egg is a basic food

explanation.surface: A dieter fighting the urge to eat, saying they keep their meals in check.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition speaks in the first person: the answer is who 'I' am.
explanation.definitionFit: A veggie is an informal word for a vegetarian, someone who limits what they eat by excluding meat.

clue.text: Refusal to admit one medical specialist's lack of experience

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the refusal word takes the other pieces inside it

blocks.note: nay is an old word for no
the Roman numeral for one
a vet is a doctor who specialises in animals

explanation.surface: A doctor who will not acknowledge they are out of their depth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Naivety is innocence or simplicity arising from never having encountered the world.

clue.text: Some awfully poor dame goes about ready to collapse?

indicators.note: 'some' points to just a portion of the following words, running across them
going about means turning round, so the run of letters is read backwards

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of awfully, all of poor and the start of dame

explanation.surface: A frail old lady in poor health who looks as if she might keel over.
explanation.walkthrough: Hidden backwards: Y POOR D read the other way gives DROOPY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something droopy sags or hangs limply, as if about to fall down; the question mark admits the stretch.

clue.text: Drunk wandering across Trafalgar Square may not be able to escape duties

blocks.clueFragment: Drunk wandering across Trafalgar Square may not be able to
blocks.note: surface reading: a tipsy reveller weaving across the square may walk straight into Nelson's monument
setter's reading: a military idiom for shirking one's work

explanation.surface: A drunk staggering about Trafalgar Square, in danger of bumping into the monument.
explanation.walkthrough: Nelson's Column stands in Trafalgar Square in London, so a drunk there may literally fail to avoid it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an old army idiom meaning to avoid one's duties or shirk work.

clue.text: Head's back in charge of company setting up place

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting up means raising, so the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: i/c is the abbreviation for in charge of
Co is the abbreviation for company
to put is to place

explanation.surface: A manager returning to run the firm and setting up base somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In charge of' looks like a phrase, but its last two words are the abbreviation i/c; 'in' merely joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The occiput is the anatomical term for the rear part of the skull.

clue.text: Impressive manner with which awards may be announced

indicators.note: something announced is spoken out, so the word is judged by its sound

blocks.note: awards handed over are gifts, which sounds like the answer

explanation.surface: A dignified bearing suits the person reading out the prizewinners at a ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Presence is a commanding or impressive bearing that makes a person noticed.

clue.text: Lad so nice, chump unfortunately lacking skill

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so these letters end up jumbled

blocks.note: fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A pleasant young man who is sadly a bit of an idiot with no talents.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unaccomplished has no particular abilities or achievements to show.

clue.text: Old tribe's gala inn arranged

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so these letters are sorted afresh

blocks.note: seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A historic tribe organising a festive party at the local pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Anglian is the adjective for the Angles, the Germanic people who settled England, so it means of that ancient tribe.

clue.text: False front potentially dangerous, taking king in

indicators.note: taking something in means enclosing it, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: dicey means risky
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A risky facade that lets royalty slip inside, like a shady front operation.
explanation.definitionFit: A dickey is a detachable shirt front worn to look like a full shirt, an imitation front.

clue.text: Similar names for a Vice President and earlier President

blocks.note: Al Gore was US Vice President under Clinton
Ike was the nickname of Dwight Eisenhower

explanation.surface: Two American politicians, a deputy and an earlier leader, whose names seem to match.
explanation.definitionFit: Alike means resembling one another, like in appearance or character.

clue.text: Various chaps seen offering an attraction for shoppers?

indicators.note: various suggests different and mixed forms, so these letters are mixed up

blocks.note: nine letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Assorted men spotted at a shop, offering something to lure in customers.
explanation.definitionFit: Low prices draw buyers into stores, so a bargain level of cost is a lure for customers.

clue.text: Half of army personnel betrayed

indicators.note: half of a word means taking just its first portion and dropping the rest

blocks.note: the first four of the eight letters of soldiers

explanation.surface: Some of the troops have been treacherously handed over to the enemy.
explanation.walkthrough: Army personnel are SOLDIERS; the first half of its eight letters is SOLD.
explanation.definitionFit: To sell someone out is to betray them, so sold can mean betrayed.

clue.text: Healthy topic to bandy about, based on a supposition

indicators.note: bandying something about means tossing it around, so these letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: twelve letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A wellness subject people love to discuss, though the evidence is mostly speculation.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypothetical describes something assumed for argument's sake rather than known to be true.

clue.text: Office worker with a measure of hotness?

blocks.note: first meaning: a stand-in secretary hired for a short period
second meaning: the short form of temperature

explanation.surface: A clerical employee who seems to be running a fever.
explanation.definitionFit: A temp is a temporary employee, and temp is also the everyday abbreviation of temperature.

clue.text: Look around Palestinian region endlessly and dream

indicators.note: without an end, the region's name loses its final letter
around means surrounding, so the looking word is wrapped about the region

blocks.note: to stare is to look fixedly
the Gaza Strip is a Palestinian territory

explanation.surface: Someone gazing across the Middle East and lost in fantasy.
explanation.walkthrough: The Gaza Strip is a Palestinian territory on the Mediterranean; 'Look' is the outer word, not the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To stargaze, besides watching the sky, is to daydream or indulge in idle fantasies.

clue.text: Amazingly good actor in crowd, part-time officer

blocks.note: an extra is a film actor hired to fill a crowd scene
a special is a special constable, a volunteer part-time police officer in Britain

explanation.surface: Praise for a remarkable performer who plays a background role and also works as a volunteer policeman.
explanation.definitionFit: Extra-special is an informal intensive meaning exceptionally fine or outstanding.

clue.text: Record a Catholic place of great activity

blocks.note: taken as written
RC stands for Roman Catholic
a hive is a busy, bustling place, from a beehive

explanation.surface: Documenting a busy Catholic establishment such as a bustling parish.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is a stored collection of historical documents, a record kept for posterity.

clue.text: Song about fellows in the country

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so the song is wrapped round the fellows

blocks.note: an aria is a solo song in opera
fellows are men

explanation.surface: A folk song about men from the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: Armenia is a nation in the Caucasus, so it is an example of a country.

clue.text: Smooth ale got drunk

indicators.note: a drunk is all over the place, so these letters stagger into a new order

blocks.note: six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A mellow beer that someone finished off.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is the musical direction for playing notes smoothly joined, without breaks.

clue.text: When groups of things will become property

blocks.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
sets are collections of matching items

explanation.surface: A musing on collections of objects turning into someone's possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: Assets are the things of value a person or company owns, their holdings.

clue.text: Old church in capital mostly attended by a learner having narrow outlook

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the capital loses its final letter
in means placed inside, so the old church goes within the capital

blocks.note: O is the abbreviation for old
CH is the abbreviation for church
the capital of France
taken as written
L is the learner-driver plate

explanation.surface: A student attending an ancient church in a big city, yet still small-minded.
explanation.walkthrough: The old church sits inside the truncated capital, not after it, so the L and A trail at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Parochial, literally of a parish, has come to mean limited in scope and provincial in attitude.

clue.text: Comes across as judge losing head, going in the wrong direction

indicators.note: losing its head means the word drops its first letter
travelling the wrong way means the letters are read from right to left

blocks.note: to esteem is to judge or consider, as in 'I esteem it an honour'

explanation.surface: A judge who has lost his composure and headed off down the wrong path.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Judge' wants to be a noun for a person in court; here it is the verb esteem, meaning to consider.
explanation.definitionFit: Meets in the sense of encounters or runs into is a straightforward synonym of comes across.

clue.text: Splendid toilet is home's number one feature

indicators.note: the number one feature of a word is its leading letter

blocks.note: lav is short for lavatory
taken as written
the first letter of home

explanation.surface: A luxurious bathroom is the showpiece of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: Lavish means richly elaborate or sumptuous, a close sense of magnificent.

clue.text: Dull male -- a Parisian, fellow from Copenhagen?

blocks.note: M is the abbreviation for male
un is French for a
Copenhagen is the capital of Denmark

explanation.surface: A boring man, perhaps a Frenchman or a Dane.
explanation.definitionFit: Mundane means ordinary and unexciting, lacking any interest.

clue.text: Story set to have a twist before the finish

indicators.note: twisting a word round means reading it the other way

blocks.note: to gel is to set, as a jelly does
the end is the finish

explanation.surface: A tale about to take a surprise turn just before it ends.
explanation.definitionFit: A legend is a traditional tale handed down, a kind of narrative.

clue.text: Renowned female, a timid sort for the most part

indicators.note: for the most part means not entirely, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for female
taken as written
a mouse is a shy, timid person

explanation.surface: A celebrated woman who is mostly shy in private.
explanation.definitionFit: Famous means widely known and celebrated, a close synonym.
